name: Ramjet
setupFrom: the compiled release: ramjet-browser archive (runtime, controller, utils) + epoxy-transport from npm at the repo's pnpm catalog pin

release.note: prebuilt release tarballs (wasm compiled with Rust nightly 1.101.0, Binaryen 132, wasm-snip 0.4.0); the Rust toolchain is not available in this env so the rewriter is not rebuilt. Artifacts are verified against the release MANIFEST/SHA256SUMS and kept under ~/.claude/stomp-work, never in the repo.

npmFrom: pnpm-workspace.yaml catalog at 452ca00c (identical pins to the scramjet contender, so transport is held constant)

serve./bench-config.js: generated by the adapter from this file

controller.ramjetConfig: the Controller's default (ramjetDefaultConfig merged with the controller partial), not the demo's defaultConfigDev debug flags
controller.codec: the controller default (encodeURIComponent under /~/sj/<controller>/<frame>/; Ramjet kept Scramjet's /~/sj/ prefix)

transport.name: epoxy
transport.where: the host page's main thread (new EpoxyTransport(options) handed to the Controller)
transport.summary: epoxy-transport 3.0.2 (npm, same build as the scramjet contender) in the host page's main thread, over the shared holyWisp

notes: Ramjet is a performance fork of Scramjet (started from 2.0.67). The browser-side API mirrors Scramjet: $ramjet + $ramjetController globals, new Controller({serviceworker, transport}), controller.wait(), controller.createFrame(el, {plugins}).

EXPRESSLY NOT USED: Ramjet's assisted transport (one server terminates upstream TLS and can read plaintext). It is a different threat model from STomp's end-to-end epoxy/holyWisp, and using it would move the transport axis. This contender uses the same epoxy-transport 3.0.2 over the same holyWisp as the scramjet contender, so scramjet-vs-ramjet isolates Ramjet's rewriter/inject/cache changes.

ramjetConfig: the Controller's own default (what bootstrap/create-ramjet-app use), not the demo's defaultConfigDev (captureErrors/debugTrampolines/debugSourceURL), which are dev aids that would slow it. Prefetch defaults off.

Built-in rewritten-OUTPUT cache (controller output-cache.ts, Cache API prefix ramjet-out-v3, x-ramjet-fresh-until, max lifetime 365 days) is always on: it caches post-rewrite script/style/image/font/manifest/track output and serves it on revisit without re-rewriting. This is Ramjet's return-visit lever. It does NOT cache top-level HTML documents.

HttpCachePlugin (ramjet-utils, ships prebuilt in the browser archive; no esbuild build needed, unlike the scramjet contender) caches upstream responses per RFC 9111; installed to match the scramjet contender.
Streaming HTML rewrite: $ramjet exports StreamingHtmlRewriter / IncrementalHtmlRewriter / createStreamingRewriter; HTML is rewritten as it streams.
transport initializes on the controller's wait()/first request (demo behaviour); the epoxy wasm compile is inside the first load after boot, same as scramjet.
no cross-origin isolation headers on the host (the demo sends none), same as the scramjet contender.
no content blocker (Ramjet, like Scramjet, has none).
